messages:
maria: FYI — ACME support reported PII processed outside EU after an automatic failover. Compliance alert (policy_exception) just hit our incident queue. Attaching quick logs below.
sam: Can you drop the tenant id and example trace?

maria: tenant=acme-corp trace=tr_9a7f
maria: log snippet:
```
[2025-10-11T14:20:31Z] trace=tr_9a7f req_id=01X header:X-Geo-Region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-east-1 handler=generate latency=118ms
[2025-10-11T14:20:31Z] audit=policy_exception tenant=acme-corp rule=data_residency_violation details="served_outside_residency"
```

ops-bot: alert: policy_exception detected (data_residency_violation) tenant=acme-corp region_expected=eu-west-1 region_served=us-east-1 severity=high :rotating_light:

ryan: We're not aware of a deliberate route change. Did a fallback policy rollout go wide?

eli: There's a recent canary that changes fallback behavior when origin latency > 80ms: fallback-policy=any-available -> might ignore residency header if under pressure.

claire: Important: need to know if persisted customer data crossed borders or only in-memory request handling. Legal needs exact timestamps and full audit.

maria: Quick repro I ran (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -H "X-Geo-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
# response headers:
#   x-serving-region: us-east-1
#   x-trace-id: tr_9a7f
```

sam: That header should have forced eu routing. If router ignored it, we need the routing decision log: /services/router/decisions/tr_9a7f

eli: Pulled the decision dump:
```
{ decision_id: dec_554, tenant: acme-corp, requested_region: eu-west-1, chosen_region: us-east-1, reason: fallback_capacity_shortage, flags: [force_cross_region=true] }
```

ryan: Who set force_cross_region=true? That's the new temporary flag we used in a performance experiment. It should not apply to tenants with residency=eu. Looks like the residency filter didn't match due to header mismatch in the tenant profile service.

maria: Also seeing increased token billing and egress on the tenant: billing spike around 14:20 UTC. billing-bot, can you confirm?

billing-bot: spike detected: tenant=acme-corp egress_bytes=2.4GB delta=+1.8GB cost_estimate=$27.30 timeframe=14:10-14:30 UTC

claire: Please capture KMS access logs for 14:10-14:30 and confirm if keys were used in non-EU region. Need this for breach/no-breach determination.

sam: Action plan: 1) freeze force_cross_region flag globally for tenants with residency constraint, 2) roll back the canary that enabled 'any-available' as default for fallbacks, 3) provide full trace + KMS logs to privacy/legal. Who can flip the flag now?

ryan: I'll flip it. Running: `./infractl feature-flag set force_cross_region false --scope=global --exclude-residency=eu`
ryan: Done. Flag state: force_cross_region=false (effective 14:22:07 UTC). :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: deploy: config rollback applied by ryan at 2025-10-11T14:22:08Z - rollback_id=rb_77a

ops-bot: compliance alert cleared for trace tr_9a7f after routing rollback. alert_status=resolved severity=low note="automated rollback reduced exposure"

maria: Shared full trace and sanitized logs with claire and legal. Uploaded to secure case: https://redwood.internal/cases/INC-2025-462 (internal link)

claire: Received. Will schedule SOC + legal review. If keys were used in non-EU region we treat as potential crossing and follow notification playbook: https://redwood.internal/playbooks/gdpr-data-exposure

eli: Root cause summary so far: canary changed fallback semantics to prefer any-available region under latency pressure. A config bug omitted residency exclusion for tenants flagged in tenant-profile; result: force_cross_region applied to eu tenants.

sam: Next steps: 1) Add unit test to tenant-profile that ensures residency attributes are honored in routing decisions, 2) add alerting for cross-region decisions for residency-scoped tenants, 3) postmortem if legal deems exposure threshold met.

ryan: I'll open infra PR to add the residency check and extra logging. tagging @eng-runtime for follow up. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/523

maria: ACME support notified and given ETA 2 hours for initial findings. They asked for a written summary.

claire: I'll draft the summary once KMS logs available. Also starting breach-assessment checklist now.

sam: Great coordinated response, thanks all. Keep this thread updated with KMS confirmation and PR link. :eyes:
